statement.p: A cone has its tip at the point (0, 0, 8) and its base the disk D, x^2+y^2\le 1, in the plane z = 1. The surface of the cone is the curved and slanted face, S, oriented upward, and the flat base, D, oriented downward. The flux of the constant vector field \vec F=a\vec i+b\vec j+c\vec k through S is given by \int_S\vec F\cdot d\vec A = 5.23.

p.em: (Enter indeterminate if it is not possible to find a value given the information provided.)

statement.p: Supposed we instead consider the vector field \vec F=a\vec i+b\vec j+c z \vec k. If we again know \int_S\vec F\cdot d\vec A = 5.23.
What is \int_D\vec F\cdot d\vec A in this case?

p.em: (Again, enter indeterminate if it is not possible to find a value given the information provided.)

static.solution:
W. The surface of W consists of S and D. Thus \int_S\vec F\cdot d\vec A+\int_D\vec F\cdot d\vec A=\int_W\mbox{div } \vec F dV. But \mbox{div }\vec F=0 everywhere, since \vec F is constant. Thus \int_D\vec F\cdot d\vec A=-\int_S\vec F\cdot d\vec A=-5.23.
In the second case, we can proceed similarly. Here \mbox{div }\vec F = c, so \int_S\vec F\cdot d\vec A+\int_D\vec F\cdot d\vec A =\int_W\mbox{div } \vec F dV = \frac{7}{3}\pi c, where we have used the fact that the volume of a cone is V = \pi r^2 h/3. Thus \int_D\vec F\cdot d\vec A= \frac{7}{3}\pi c -\int_S\vec F\cdot d\vec A= \frac{7}{3}\pi c - 5.23.
